config.title: Write a first non repeating character finder

intro.title: Write a first non repeating character finder
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that finds the first non-repeating character in a given string. You will learn to use objects (or maps) to count character frequencies, a common technique for tracking data. The core programming concept involves iterating through strings and using conditional logic to identify unique characters. You'll practice with fundamental JavaScript constructs like loops, objects, and string methods to solve this lesson step by step.
intro.usecase: Finding the first non-repeating character is essential in text processing and validation scenarios. For instance, when building a search engine's autocomplete feature, you might need to identify unique characters to optimize indexing or highlight distinct terms. In form validation, this algorithm can detect unusual patterns in usernames or passwords by analyzing character frequency. It's also used in data analysis dashboards to process log files or user input streams, helping identify anomalies or unique entries in large datasets.

objectives: Initialize a frequency counter object to track character occurrences in a string
Apply a loop to populate the frequency counter with character counts
Construct a second loop to identify the first character with a count of one
Implement a function that returns the first non-repeating character or a fallback value
Manipulate string input to handle edge cases like empty strings or all repeating characters
Integrate the character finder function with a simple test interface
Configure the solution to handle both lowercase and uppercase characters appropriately
